rules.rule: Check for urgent signs at initial assessment of the patient
rules.problem: Covers all 21 red-box items plus the management-line inputs (unable to sit up, known diabetic) and the routine-box cough, pregnancy and diabetes triggers. Every extra item is consumed by a task due_to. A generic Clinical finding trigger fits a page that applies to every patient.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure glucose if decreased consciousness, seizures, confused, unable to sit up or diabetic
rules.problem: Faithful to management line 2. The house standard says glucose is a routine vital that needs no measure task, so this task may be redundant, but it is not wrong. It omits the red-box gate (the page applies it to urgent patients); harmless.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure respiratory rate and oxygen saturation if coughing or difficulty breathing
rules.problem: Faithful to the routine box. RR and SpO2 are routine vitals by the house standard, so the task is arguably unnecessary. 'If available' is dropped.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure MUAC and height in the pregnant patient
rules.problem: The page limits MUAC and height to the booking visit; the rule fires on every pregnancy visit. Weight is routine anyway. Hb, rhesus/syphilis and urine dipstick are not measurements, so leaving them out is acceptable.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure BMI inputs, waist circumference and glucose in the patient with hypertension
rules.problem: The page sets BMI, waist and glucose once a year (waist 3-6 monthly if losing weight); the rule fires every visit with no cadence. The concepts are right.

rules.rule: Initial assessment: measure glucose, BMI inputs, waist and hip circumference in the patient with diabetes
rules.problem: Glucose is every visit, but BMI, waist and hip (waist-hip ratio) are once a year; the cadence is collapsed into one every-visit task. The concepts are right.

Urgent matches 'Give urgent attention'. All 21 red-box criteria are present. 'Headache and vomiting' is correctly an and. 'Pregnant with abdominal pain/vaginal bleeding' is correctly and(pregnancy, or(...)). The rash is split into an or of Non-blanching and Purpuric, which is equivalent because purpura is non-blanching. No presenting-complaint and-wrapper is used, which is right for a page that applies to all patients.

rules.rule: (missing) Seen promptly by nurse or doctor
rules.problem: The middle box 'Ensure the patient with any of the following is seen promptly by nurse or doctor' is page triage logic and has no rule: BP >= 180/110 or systolic < 80, pregnant with BP >= 140/90, pulse irregular/>= 100/< 50, temperature >= 38, glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) or >= 11.1, SpO2 < 92% at rest, or a drop to < 87% on exertion. RR >= 30 appears only through the Urgent rule.

summary: The concepts are clean: every red-box criterion maps to an existing, appropriate SNOMED concept, and the and/or structure of the Urgent rule matches the page. The most consequential gap is that the 'seen promptly by nurse or doctor' vital-sign box (BP, pulse, temperature, glucose and SpO2 thresholds) has no priority rule. The measure tasks also lose the page's timing: MUAC and height are for the booking visit only, and BMI, waist and hip are once a year. 'Suspected fracture' is encoded as a confirmed fracture.
